question: A 7-year-old girl comes in to the emergency department with her mother for swelling of her left periorbital region. Yesterday morning she woke up with a painful, warm, soft lump on her left eyelid. Eye movement does not worsen the pain. Physical examination shows redness and swelling of the upper left eyelid, involving the hair follicles. Upon palpation, the swelling drains purulent fluid. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Infection of the hair follicles -> Painful, warm, soft lump on the eyelid -> Swelling and redness of the upper eyelid -> Purulent fluid drainage upon palpation -> Hordeolum -> 95%

CHAIN: Infection of the hair follicles -> Painful, warm, soft lump on the eyelid -> Swelling and redness of the upper eyelid -> Purulent fluid drainage upon palpation -> Hordeolum -> Dacryocystitis -> 80%
analysis: Based on the presentation of a painful, warm, soft lump on the left eyelid with redness and swelling involving hair follicles, along with purulent drainage upon palpation, the most likely diagnosis is a Hordeolum, also known as a stye. A hordeolum is a common bacterial infection of the eyelid glands.
